output.body:
# A consent notification to an HIU bridge

## In plain words

When a patient decides on your consent request, ABDM posts the decision to your [HIU](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#hiu) bridge at `/api/v3/hiu/consent/request/notify`. The path is relative to the callback URL you registered. Acknowledge each notification by calling [consent HIU on-notify](/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m3/endpoints/m3-consent-management-data-flow-hiu/03-m3-post-consent-v3-request-hiu-on-notify).

## Before you start

A callback URL registered for your bridge and reachable from the public internet.

## What happens

ABDM posts with the `REQUEST-ID`, `TIMESTAMP` and `X-HIU-ID` headers, and expects 200 OK. Then acknowledge on `/api/hiecm/consent/v3/request/hiu/on-notify`, with this notification's `REQUEST-ID` as `requestId`.

## When it goes wrong

No notification arrives: check that the callback URL is public, registered and quick to answer. Make the handler idempotent on `consentRequestId` and `status`.

reply.Text:
Found it. The issue is **idempotency**. From the consent notify callback documentation:

> Make the handler idempotent on `consentRequestId` and `status`.

The gateway is retrying the same callback (likely due to network timing or its own retry logic), but your handler isn't checking if you've already processed this exact notification. Even though you're returning 200 correctly, you're probably reprocessing the callback each time it arrives.

**Fix:** Before processing the callback, check if you've already handled a notification for this `consentRequestId` with this same `status`. If you have, just return 200 without doing anything else.

For example, track in your database:
```
(consentRequestId, status) → already processed
```

When a callback arrives, check that composite key first. If it exists, return 200 immediately. Only process it if you haven't seen that pair before.

This is from the HIE-CM v3 consent notify callback documentation at `/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m3/endpoints/m3-callbacks/03-m3-post-v3-hiu-consent-request-notify`.
